## Design

### 2026-10-08 – At the start of this project I wanted to not only  better my github skills but also learn the proper development cycle of a project . This meant that I started my research with simple goals based on m

**6h**

At the start of this project I wanted to not only  better my github skills but also learn the proper development cycle of a project . This meant that I started my research with simple goals based on my original project idea and constraints I knew I wanted.
![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 20.24.15](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/b3524b30ec0b1aee52ec1cc96d1e5ff8a2fb67d88ebf48d0aabcf651d052906a.png)

From there I took time to look into what my own goals meant - from the requirements of the MCU that I chose to the specifics of other Xiao boards and around that I drew up some nice looking design requirements!

Sorted into sections of Electrical

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 20.23.31](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/76338f1f128f184af5d8a259b012c887493e7f51c81bab0593af36e61b0c5b00.png)
![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 20.29.56](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/27dd7b73a79edb0250471d132caa038b08caa4da9f4e5cc79a0d1becb2279610.png)
To Mechanical

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 20.23.42](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/690a085ae56b3e920cc0b1dc7bd3ee20f4c106dc20cdd01bf52d59563095c2ce.png)

To Interface

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 20.23.57](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/fabb47365bba9c23a794603f0d3cc1056506b21c6e67e37e8a05128a563988e0.png)

And Manufacturing

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 at 20.24.03](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/e6dd5106242a137c78233c042c5a87b3b2df4f13dfdced67323346c707331fb7.png)

Reading the long datasheet of my MCU did take a while and trying to understand it fully so I can make a project that works first try was paramount to me.

I really hope to be able to fit the entire battery circuitry on the board as well as i have put a bit of time into thinking that through as well but it remains to see if I have space for it once I choose the components finish the schematic and start laying out the board.

### 2026-10-09 – Having a full day to work on this project before the end of the week I got to work turning my design rules into a product! This starts of course with finding parts to match my goals. First a suitable

**8h**

Having a full day to work on this project before the end of the week I got to work turning my design rules into a product! This starts of course with finding parts to match my goals. First a suitable LDO :
![Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 00.01.56](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/d92cacbb6a4c2992df9718a8ce60797dd77f7e383cdad21371fd64ee983745f8.png)
Again trying to meet the low quiescent current requirements and size goals (we get back to this later today as my goals began to clash)
Then since I really wanted a on board battery charging solution I had to find a charging chip:
![Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 00.02.04](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/0e5274d72b4caed0eb2949fa1bcaa609d5700fbba802a7e767a82a4bf10e2934.png)
Taking guidance from the included typical application sheets and a bit of extra googling to add some safety and "idiotproofness" I ended up with a first schematic!
![Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 00.08.27](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/e634033e6721caf4384a9d55b77dcf7cd4b92b26752f3982f38f9fa213491998.png)
This is a later nce since my saving habits are so terrible but what this then showed me once I placed just the MCU and USBC on the board that I had no space...
![Screenshot 2026-10-09 at 23.46.11](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/44b40ca42df2311cdd7596da7878badb1596828834c842da9218cd2f45ef5b92.png)

looking back it should be obvious that my goals of hand solderability and small form factor were fundamentally clashing. I went down a small rabbit hole of making the charging components a " hat" to my board but I was still always gonna be lacking space- so I had to decide to adjust  my goals/requirements.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 at 23.42.30](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/c36d2658e8d6d41722f910cd25abf758b53bf99c2f7cd8b005ec1c921f5efefd.png)

The new sizing I created as an independent component ( if I need my own dev board in future products) giving it 36 pins to allow the whole chip to be accessed and provide plenty of gnd and 3v3 for easy use on breadboards. The width is still the same as the xiao so call this the xiao long way :0
![Screenshot 2026-10-09 at 23.43.49](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/d75d969a21f5bcafbda5640a5b19d61faa413ffbd80aba9e0dad3dacd095cc26.png)
Then finally I got to sit and start routing( obviously the board is as small as can be to fit all 36 pins so this not easy- and also not done )

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 at 23.45.15](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/c58787288f02890dde9dc6abe985920dc9b61fe1a680044b3d356683d2c18d5a.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 at 23.44.50](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/bf521211970ba97aafda2d09f9a9fd85a433486c0ca283e476132e01326358f1.png)
